claims.text: Rapid solidification will refine the grain size of the magnetic high-entropy alloy.
Rapid solidification will increase the grain-boundary density of the magnetic high-entropy alloy.
The conventionally solidified baseline has coarser grains than the rapidly solidified material.
The conventionally solidified baseline has a lower grain-boundary density than the rapidly solidified material.
Grain boundaries act as pinning sites for magnetic domain walls.
Increasing grain-boundary density increases the energy required for domain-wall motion.
Impeded domain-wall motion raises the coercive field.
The rapidly solidified, fine-grained alloy will have a higher coercive field than the composition-matched, conventionally solidified coarse-grained baseline.
The predicted coercivity increase should hold when domain-wall motion is the dominant coercivity mechanism.
The predicted effect should hold when grain-boundary density can be increased without introducing excessive defects or amorphous phases.
The hypothesis is intended to apply at room temperature to polycrystalline bulk samples of identical alloy composition.
The magnitude of the coercive-field increase may depend on the alloy system and processing parameters.
